subject: brain
topic: Long-term stress leaves a mark on the brain
angle: While some experiments show chronic stress reduces hippocampal volume, other studies show it may have no effect on volume or even lead to volume increases in resilient subjects.
title: The Architecture of Stress

hooks.text: Does stress always change your brain?
You assume stress shrinks your brain. Evidence is mixed.
You are letting your stress dictate your biology.
A flickering light in a quiet room.
The physical mark of chronic stress.

reveal.headline: Chronic stress does not always shrink your brain.
reveal.body: While some studies show reduced hippocampal volume, others show no effect or even volume increases in resilient subjects.

explain.headline: The brain responds differently to pressure.
explain.body: Chronic stress can cause hippocampal atrophy and reduced glycogen content. However, some resilient subjects show increased volume. Results vary by stressor type and individual susceptibility.

matters.headline: Resilience is not a constant state.
matters.body: That may be why your reaction to pressure feels unpredictable. Your brain structure might be adapting in ways that are not uniform or visible to everyone.

example.headline: A heavy work week.
example.body: You sit at your desk late into the evening. Your pulse stays high even after you close your laptop. You feel the weight of the day in your head.

question.headline: How does your brain adapt to the pressure you choose?

stat.label: change in left hippocampal volume in resilient subjects

claims.text: Chronic unpredictable mild stress failed to affect hippocampal volume in rats.
claims.quote: Moreover, we found an increased hippocampal volume in rats exposed to CMS after clomipramine treatment while CMS failed to affect hippocampal volume.

claims.text: Chronic social defeat stress caused a significant increase in left hippocampal volume in resilient mice, but not in susceptible mice.
claims.quote: After chronic social defeat stress, we found significant increases in left hippocampal volume in resilient and nonstressed control mice. Intriguingly, this increase in hippocampal volume was not found in susceptible mice

claims.text: No association was observed between maternal cortisol in pregnancy and child hippocampus volume in either sex.
claims.quote: No association between maternal cortisol in pregnancy and child hippocampus volume was observed in either sex.

claims.text: Chronic stress-induced atrophy of hippocampal astrocyte size is associated with decreased glycogen content.
claims.quote: Results suggest that decreased glycogen content was associated with chronic stress-induced atrophy of hippocampal astrocyte size and depression-like behavior.

claims.text: Prolactin protects neurogenesis in the dentate gyrus of chronically stressed mice and promotes neuronal fate.
claims.quote: The results demonstrate that PRL protects neurogenesis in the DG of chronically stressed mice and promotes neuronal fate.

claims.text: Chronic stress causes a reduction in hippocampal volume.
claims.quote: Chronic exposure to stress results in a reduction of hippocampal neurogenesis and of hippocampal volume.

verdict: The evidence is mixed, showing that chronic stress can reduce hippocampal volume in some contexts but does not consistently cause it across all subjects or conditions.
caveat: The findings vary significantly depending on the specific type of stressor, the species studied, and whether the subjects are susceptible or resilient to the stress.
caption:
Chronic stress leaves a mark on the brain, but the shape of that mark is not fixed. 

Research shows mixed results. While some studies link stress to reduced hippocampal volume, others find no change or even volume increases in resilient subjects. These findings vary by stressor and individual susceptibility.

How do you perceive your own resilience to daily stress?
